preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 5000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and 1 <= n <= 5000 for n in ns)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the length n is an integer between 1 and 5000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(s, str) and len(s) == n and all(c.islower() and c.isalpha() for c in s) for n, s in zip(ns, ss))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the string s has length n and consists only of lowercase Latin letters.
The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 5000.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly 2 lines per test case.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_lines[2*i] == transform_string(s, k) and stdout_lines[2*i+1] == str(k) for i, (n, s) in enumerate(zip(ns, ss)) for k in [best_k(n, s)])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the first output line is the string resulting from applying the modification with the optimal k, and the second line is that optimal k.

postconditions.expression: all(transform_string(s, best_k(n, s)) <= transform_string(s, k) for i, (n, s) in enumerate(zip(ns, ss)) for k in range(1, n+1))
postconditions.description: The chosen k yields a string that is lexicographically smaller than or equal to the string produced by any other valid k.

postconditions.expression: all(best_k(n, s) == min([k for k in range(1, n+1) if transform_string(s, k) == transform_string(s, best_k(n, s))]) for n, s in zip(ns, ss))
postconditions.description: Among all k that produce the lexicographically smallest string, the chosen k is the smallest.
